_about: Which mocap skeletons the viewer can put on a generated character, as data (HAM-316).
Adding a vendor is adding a profile here. No C++ changes, as long as the vendor's bones
have no rotation in its T-pose once each is written relative to its parent; both
vendors below do. Read by LoomaLiveLinkProfiles.cpp when the first character is driven.
bones:     rig bone (the 22 body bones of LoomaMixamo-A/1) -> the Live Link bone that drives it.
A rig bone left out keeps its T-pose rotation relative to its parent.
boneAxes:  the performer's left, up and forward in a source bone's OWN coordinates, in the T-pose.
worldAxes: the same three directions in the source's world, for a performer facing its default way.
source:    optional. Part of a Live Link source's type, as the Live Link panel shows it. A profile
with one is only for subjects of such a source, and is preferred for them: it is how two
sources that send the same bone names differently are told apart.
rootRotation: optional, x y z w. A rotation the source put in front of its root bone's own, taken
off again before the pose is read.
like:      optional. The name of another profile whose bones and axes this one uses unless it
A subject uses the profile for its source if there is one, else the first profile without a
'source', among those all of whose 'required' rig bones it has.

profiles.name: moverse
profiles.about: Moverse (SMPL, 24 joints), as code/moverse-simulation-python sends it. Bone-local: X left, Y down, Z forward. World: Unreal's, with the performer facing +Y.

profiles.name: moverse-plugin
profiles.about: The same stream read by Moverse's own Unreal plugin (MoversePlugin) instead of the viewer's reader. The plugin turns the root bone a quarter turn about X before pushing it (rot90 * BoneQuat in MoversePluginSource.cpp) and leaves its translation alone, so a character read with the 'moverse' profile lies on its back. Taking the quarter turn off again gives exactly the 'moverse' stream.

profiles.name: xsens
profiles.about: Xsens MVN (23 segments), as the MVN network protocol sends it and LoomaMvnLiveLinkSource reads it. Bone-local and world alike: X forward, Y left, Z up. Xsens has four spine segments and the rig three, so T12 drives nothing.
